text: CHAPTER 14
speaker: Narrator

text: The Man Who Already Knew
speaker: Narrator
note: Chapter title. Leave a clean beat before story begins.

text: The Collector found them before they finished packing for the east-side survey.
speaker: Narrator

text: He was waiting in the narrow lane behind the cheap room, leaning against the wall like a man who had all morning and no intention of wasting it on politeness. Two temple guards stood a short distance away, looking bored in the specific way of men paid to look dangerous. The Collector himself looked almost regretful. That bothered Zik more than anger would have.
speaker: Narrator

text: You've been busy,
speaker: The Collector

text: the Collector said.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Balag's hand drifted toward the haft of his axe and then stopped. Enhedu's expression went carefully blank. Ninsun simply watched, stylus still in her fingers from the map she had been updating.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik set the pack down.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: We're taking a paying job. East side. Walls that need measuring. Nothing that should interest you.
speaker: Zik

text: Everything you do interests me lately.
speaker: The Collector

text: The Collector's eyes moved across the four of them, lingering a fraction too long on the linen around Zik's left hand and the satchel where Ninsun kept her scraps.
speaker: Narrator

text: Notches in walls that officially don't exist. Questions about blank tablets. A certain district that keeps appearing on no one's maps but yours. You've drawn attention.
speaker: The Collector

text: From who?
speaker: Balag

text: Balag asked.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: The Collector almost smiled.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: From people who prefer their attention not to be noticed in return.
speaker: The Collector

text: Enhedu tilted her head.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: You're not here to buy.
speaker: Enhedu

text: No.
speaker: The Collector

text: He looked at Zik.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: I'm here because your father made the same mistake you're making now. He thought the City was a puzzle that wanted to be solved. It isn't. It's a lid. And lids exist to keep something from rising. The more you mark it, the more you tell it exactly where the curious ones are standing.
speaker: The Collector

text: Ninsun's voice was quiet.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: You know about the marks.
speaker: Ninsun

text: I know about the ones who made them before you. Most of them stopped. A few didn't. The ones who didn't are why certain drawers in the lower archives stay locked.
speaker: The Collector

text: He glanced at the two guards, then back.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: I'm offering you the same chance I offered your father. Walk away from the shifted streets. Take the east-side work. Take the silver. Let the lid stay closed.
speaker: The Collector

text: Zik held his stare.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: And if we don't?
speaker: Zik

text: The Collector's expression didn't change.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Then you'll learn, the same way he did, that some prices are paid in advance. And some debts collect themselves.
speaker: The Collector

text: He pushed off the wall, adjusted the sleeve of his robe, and walked away. The guards fell in behind him without being told. At the end of the lane he paused, just long enough to look back once.
speaker: Narrator

text: Your father finally understood he had been asking the wrong question,
speaker: The Collector

text: he said.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: I hope you're smarter than he was. Or luckier. I'm not certain which one matters more.
speaker: The Collector

text: Then he was gone.
speaker: Narrator

text: The lane felt smaller after he left.
speaker: Narrator

text: Balag exhaled through his nose.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: I fucking hate that man.
speaker: Balag

text: He's not wrong about the attention,
speaker: Enhedu

text: Enhedu said. She was already recalculating something behind her eyes.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: We've been loud in places that prefer quiet.
speaker: Enhedu

text: Ninsun looked down at the map still half-open in her hands. The boxes labeled CLAIMED, COST, and LIMIT sat in a tight cluster near the tanners' row.
speaker: Narrator

text: He knew about the marks. He knew about the ones who came before us. That means the locked drawers have names in them. Or the absence of names.
speaker: Ninsun

text: Zik picked up the pack. The journal inside it had not been opened in nine days. The decision still felt like the only clean thing he owned.
speaker: Narrator

text: We take the east-side job,
speaker: Zik

text: he said.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: We get paid. We watch who watches us. And we don't cut another notch until we know whether the Collector is warning us or herding us.
speaker: Zik

text: No one argued.
speaker: Narrator

text: They walked out of the lane in the order that had become habit. Behind them the cheap room and the map and the accumulating scraps of evidence waited like a second set of lungs the city had not yet decided to collapse.
speaker: Narrator
